summary: I sent the exact prompt once and didn't need any follow-ups. The agent loaded hyperpowers:writing-plans and read the spec, the source, the tests and src/ui. It then wrote docs/hyperpowers/plans/2026-10-02-deploys-page.md (369 lines). The page code in the plan builds the Deploys page from the src/ui library (dataTable, selectField, filterBar, statusChip, emptyState, pageHeader). The plan says plainly that it does not copy the hand-written services.js. No source, test, data or public file was changed.
reasoning: All four criteria passed, each checked against the files on disk, git status and the session log. The plan builds the table and the filter with the library's dataTable and selectField and explicitly turns down copying services.js. No implementation files were touched.

observations.description: The first-run trust and bypass-permissions dialogs both start with "No, exit" selected, so I had to press Down before Enter. This is Claude Code onboarding, not the skill.
docs/hyperpowers/ is gitignored in this repo, so the plan can't be committed. The agent pointed this out in its summary, which is good.

The Codex review gate couldn't run: "codex-plugin-cc isn't installed ... plugin registry not found". The agent logged it as a skipped gate in the review ledger and told the user. Its first preflight attempt also guessed the plugin root path wrong (CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT / cache glob) before it retried with the real path.
The agent ran the plan's code in a scratch copy of the repo (32 tests passed) without touching the workdir. That checks the plan well, but it goes a little beyond 'just write the plan'.

Where the spec left room, the agent listed the choices it made (the All-environments value, the default sort direction for each column, durations shown without rolling over into hours, e.g. '75m 0s'). That makes the plan easy to review.

criteria.evidence: Screen: "⏺ Skill(hyperpowers:writing-plans) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill". The session log's first tool_use is "Skill hyperpowers:writing-plans".

criteria.criterion: Plan document exists under docs/hyperpowers/plans/ or docs/superpowers/plans/
Plan's page code calls dataTable and selectField, not hand-written <table>/<select>
criteria.evidence: Plan line 195: "import { dataTable, emptyState, filterBar, pageHeader, selectField, statusChip } from '../ui/index.js';". Line 224 calls `selectField({ name: 'env', ...})` and line 237 calls `const table = dataTable({ columns: COLUMNS, rows: deploys, sort, sortHref, empty: emptyState(...) })`. I grepped for `<table` and `<select`. The only matches are test assertions: line 142 checks the library's output (`<select name="env" class="ui-select"`) and line 168 is `assert.doesNotMatch(html, /<table/)`, which covers the empty state. Line 9 of the plan says the page is built from src/ui and is "not by copying the hand-rolled HTML ... in src/pages/services.js".

criteria.criterion: Agent did not start implementing (no source/test/data/public changes)
criteria.evidence: `git status --porcelain --ignored` shows only "!! docs/" (ignored). `git diff --stat HEAD` is empty, and HEAD is still 34345a2. The log shows a single Write, to the plan file. The agent did check the plan's code by copying the repo into a mktemp scratch directory and running tests there, not in the workdir.
